races.title: State House, District 35
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mike Schietzelt
cands.bio: Republican state House member for District 35 (Wake County) from 2025. Attorney and Marine Corps veteran (2011-2015) with a Duke law degree. Former law clerk to NC Chief Justice Mark Martin, John Locke Foundation fellow, Regent University law fellow, and litigator at Michael Best & Friedrich.

endorsements.text: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he named the NC Values Coalition and Americans for Prosperity as endorsers (self-reported). Ballotpedia says it did not independently identify endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find when his family moved to North Carolina. We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, limits on out-of-state, investor or foreign land buyers, gun laws, abortion, or the homestead property tax specifically. His claims about votes and bills come from his own campaign materials and were not confirmed against bill records. We also found no reporting on controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says he was born in Escondido, California, and raised in Burlington, NC, where he graduated from Western Alamance High School in 2004; Ballotpedia also lists Western Alamance High School.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served one term in the NC House (2025-2026). Attorney with a Duke JD (2018), clerk to the NC Chief Justice, Criminal Justice Fellow at the John Locke Foundation (2019-20), Regent University constitutional law fellow and lecturer, and litigator at Michael Best & Friedrich since 2022.
qual.why: Prior legislative service plus a law and policy career fits the high band for writing law and the budget. He has only one term in office, so the score sits at the lower end of that band.
qual.label: Prior legislative service plus a law and policy career fits the high band for writing law and the budget. He has only one term in office, so the score sits at the lower end of that band.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he voted to override the Governor's veto of HB 318, which requires sheriffs and detention facilities to cooperate with ICE detainer requests for people charged with felonies and serious misdemeanors. This is the campaign's own description and was not checked against a roll call.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: In his 2026 Ballotpedia survey he said he supported constitutional amendments to slow property tax growth and cap the state income tax, and sponsored legislation to eliminate sales taxes on groceries and other family items.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he sponsored the LSAU Open Enrollment Act, supported HB 87 (opting NC into a federal tax-credit scholarship program), and co-sponsored bipartisan legislation for an average 22% teacher raise that was included in the House budget.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Evonne S. Hopkins
cands.bio: Board Certified Family Law Specialist and owner of the Raleigh Law Center. She holds a JD/MBA from the University of San Francisco and is licensed in North Carolina, California and D.C. She volunteers with The Child's Advocate. Ran for NC House District 35 in 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: In her 2024 Ballotpedia survey she reported endorsements from EMILY's List, Planned Parenthood Votes! South Atlantic, Lillian's List, NCAE, NC League of Conservation Voters, NCAAT, Equality NC, NC Sierra Club and AFL-CIO. These are self-reported for the 2024 race.
For 2026 Ballotpedia lists Work For Democracy and several Sway voting-group guides, including NC Public School Champions and YALLvote.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Hopkins was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. She has not held public office, so there is no record of bills or actions in office. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, immigration or H-1B, or school vouchers. Her site says she respects the Second Amendment and wants to keep guns away from children and people who pose a threat, but it names no specific gun policy. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and her 2024 survey answers are the only other statements of her views.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Family law attorney since about 2003 (JD/MBA), Board Certified Family Law Specialist, and owner and operator of the Raleigh Law Center. She has not held elected office.
qual.why: Lawyer and small-business owner, which fits the middle band. No prior legislative service, policy-staff work or budget career was found.
qual.label: Lawyer and small-business owner, which fits the middle band. No prior legislative service, policy-staff work or budget career was found.

pro-life.evidence: Her campaign site says reproductive healthcare decisions belong with patients, their families and their doctors, not politicians in the General Assembly.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says North Carolina must raise teacher pay and invest in counselors, nurses and special-education staff in public schools. It takes no position on vouchers or charters.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site says growth is good but must be planned, that new growth should help pay for the infrastructure it requires, and that development should not overwhelm streams and water systems. It also says she does not want to stop growth.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site lists supporting law enforcement and first responders, investing in mental health care and preventing violence as part of her safer-communities platform.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site: 'Growth is good, but we have to plan for it.' She wants infrastructure to keep pace and new growth to help pay for the resources it requires, and says she doesn't want to stop growth. She also names protecting clean drinking water and tree canopy.
